_comment: Coverage ratchet floor (W1-T25, MASTER-PLAN §5 TIER 2 gate 1/4). Captured from remudero's own test suite (src/** only, test/** excluded) via `node --enable-source-maps --experimental-test-coverage --test-coverage-exclude=test/** --test-reporter=lcov`. Never lower these numbers to make a PR pass -- raise them (ratchet up) when coverage genuinely improves; a coverage-lowering PR must go CI-red on scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs. EXACTLY ONE EXCEPTION EXISTS AND IT MUST BE PROVEN, NEVER ARGUED: a DENOMINATOR SHIFT, where BRF rose because the suite DISCOVERED more branches -- not because covered branches became uncovered. THE BURDEN IS ON THE LOWERING PR AND IT IS DELIBERATELY EXPENSIVE. To lower a floor, the PR body must state ALL FIVE of: (1) BRF before and after, as RAW COUNTS, never percentages; (2) BRH before and after, as raw counts; (3) that BRH DID NOT FALL -- if BRH fell this is a REGRESSION and the exception does not apply, whatever else moved; (4) the RATIO of the two moves, because a discovery-driven shift moves BRF by a large multiple of BRH (#1739 moved BRF +204 against BRH +107); (5) how many WHOLE-SUITE readings each figure rests on and their spread -- at least three, one tree, CI's exact invocation, each with a `# tests` summary line, discarding any reading whose test count differs from its siblings. A REVIEWER WHO WAS NOT PRESENT MUST REFUSE ON ANY MISSING ITEM. A claim quoting only percentages, or asserting merely that `the denominator moved`, or resting on a single reading, IS NOT EVIDENCE: `it is a denominator shift` is the cheapest available story for anyone who wants a red PR to land, and the person telling it is always the person who wants it to land.
_rebased: 2026-08-11 (after #1564, W1-T421): the 82.75/88.55 floor below had stopped describing this suite, and the gate was permitting a ~13-point regression without noticing. TWO CAUSES, AND ONLY ONE IS A DEFECT. (1) STALENESS: the floor was set 2026-07-22 and never ratcheted through three weeks of coverage work. (2) A MEASUREMENT DEFECT, from 2026-08-10 (#1527) to 2026-08-11 (#1564): two falsifier suites wrote a mutated module copy to os.tmpdir() and imported it, whose graph re-entered the real src/lib from outside the project root, and the aggregate read 84.19% instead of 96.18%. The floor was HONEST WHEN SET -- the construct's first appearance anywhere in test/ is 295d2d3 (2026-08-10), 19 days after the floor, established by running #1564's tmpdirModuleImports detector over the tree at all 422 commits that touched test/ since the baseline commit. So this is drift plus a one-day defect, not a floor that was never real. THREE READINGS on b6d13e3, same tree, same flags: lines 96.1814 / 96.1927 / 96.1814, branches 90.5924 / 90.5864 / 90.5460 -- a 0.011pt lines spread and a 0.046pt branches spread, so ~96.18 is stable rather than a single post-fix reading. THE MARGIN IS THE EXISTING CONVENTION, NOT AN INVENTED ONE: the 2026-07-22 floor sat 0.08 (lines) / 0.06 (branches) under the LOWER of its two contemporaneous readings and 0.56 / 0.10 under the HIGHER, explicitly so a cross-environment delta never reads as a regression. All three readings here are LOCAL -- no CI reading was obtainable (the #1564 job log returned 404) -- so the WORST-CASE margin the old floor carried is applied to the LOWEST local reading: 96.1814 - 0.56 -> 95.62, 90.5460 - 0.10 -> 90.44. This matters because evaluateRatchet compares at epsilon 1e-9, i.e. zero tolerance: a hundredth of a point below the floor is a red gate, so the margin is load-bearing, not decoration. WHAT IT STILL CATCHES: at LF 88436 the remaining slack is ~496 lines, against ~11,877 under the old floor -- the gate is ~24x tighter than before this change, not looser. A re-basing, not a regression.
_branchFloorCorrection: BRANCH FLOOR CORRECTED 2026-08-11, same day, after #1566: 90.44 -> 90.40. THE LINE FLOOR IS NOT TOUCHED. The correction is to the MARGIN, not to the measurement: #1566 set the branch floor 0.10 under its lowest reading on the strength of a 0.046pt spread it attributed to the FLAKY-TEST COUNT, reasoning that a test failing early executes fewer branches. THAT ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTION AND MECHANISM. Four fresh runs on ONE tree (09c7bda), same flags: branches 90.5764 (fail 11), 90.5158 (fail 10), 90.5750 (fail 10), 90.6094 (fail 10). THREE RUNS AT AN IDENTICAL FAIL COUNT SPREAD 0.0936pt -- wider than the entire 0.046pt spread flake count was blamed for -- so flake count explains none of it, and the highest reading of all came from a run with the FEWEST failures, the opposite of the claim. THE DRIVER IS THE DENOMINATOR: across those four runs BRH moves by 2 (12176-12178) while BRF moves by 15 (13439-13454). A run that loads fewer modules discovers fewer branches, and since the undiscovered ones are mostly uncovered, dropping them RAISES the ratio. THE MARGIN WAS SMALLER THAN THE NOISE IT EXISTS TO ABSORB: 90.5158 - 90.44 = 0.0758pt against a measured 0.0936pt spread, i.e. 0.81x. A gate comparing at epsilon 1e-9 was sitting three quarters of a noise band from a healthy run. 90.40 sits 0.1158pt under the lowest of eight local readings = 1.24x the measured spread, and gives up ~16 branches out of BRF 13445 -- MEASURED both directions against the real gate: 90.3895% (17 branches removed) BLOCKS at -0.01pts, 90.4043% (15 removed) is ACCEPTED, and 89.8989% BLOCKS at -0.50pts -- the control proves the block is the floor and not the fixture. THE LINE FLOOR NEEDS NO CORRECTION: its margin is 0.5569pt against a 0.0135pt spread, 41x, so the same arithmetic that condemns the branch margin exonerates the line one. AND THIS IS NOT CHASING A CI RED: #1566's own coverage-ratchet job has since printed lines 96.25% / branches 90.59%, both ABOVE the floors it was tested against -- CI reads HIGHER than local, so the correction buys headroom against LOCAL noise, which is where the whole margin is consumed.
_recaptured: RE-CAPTURED 2026-08-13 (W1-T467 option 1, operator ruling): lines 95.62 -> 97.75, branches 90.40 -> 90.02. THE LINE FLOOR TIGHTENS 2.13pt AND THE BRANCH FLOOR LOOSENS 0.38pt -- MIXED, not a pure ratchet-up, said plainly rather than sold as an improvement. WHY THE BRANCH FLOOR MAY BE LOWERED AT ALL -- the _comment exception, satisfied item by item: #1739 (W1-T460) widened the import graph; BRF rose ~+204 while BRH rose ~+107, so BRH DID NOT FALL and the ratio is ~1.9:1 discovery-to-coverage; src/lib/deployer.ts is BYTE-IDENTICAL across the two shas yet gained countable untaken arms of `newPid ?? null`, `data ? ... : ""` and `...(data ?? {})` inside code six test files already call. NEWLY COUNTED, NOT NEWLY BROKEN. READINGS: three whole-suite runs on ONE pinned tree (fe7d1bc4) on the mac mini, CI's exact invocation through scripts/test-with-retry.mjs with the spec reporter, all three at tests 6811 (fail 4-5, host-only: GNU `date -d` and the login keychain, both green in CI): lines 98.3205 / 98.3267 / 98.3349 (spread 0.0144pt), branches 90.3292 / 90.3351 / 90.3595 (spread 0.0303pt). CROSS-CHECKED against 30 uncontended CI coverage-ratchet runs post-#1739: lines 98.31..98.34, branches 90.12..90.28. THE MARGIN IS THIS FILE'S OWN CONVENTION (0.56 lines / 0.10 branches under the LOWEST reading) APPLIED TO THE LOWEST ATTESTED READING FROM EITHER ENVIRONMENT, which is CI's: 98.31 - 0.56 -> 97.75, 90.12 - 0.10 -> 90.02. THE CHANGE OF BASIS IS DELIBERATE AND THE REASON MATTERS: _rebased below assumed `CI reads HIGHER than local`, and THAT HAS INVERTED -- local now reads 90.33 against CI's 90.12..90.28 -- so a local-only basis would have set the branch floor at 90.22, ABOVE CI's own observed minimum, and left main red in the only environment the gate actually runs in. BOTH DIRECTIONS MEASURED against the real gate on a real main lcov: all three readings PASS the new floors and all three BLOCK the old ones; degrading that same lcov, 46 branches removed (90.03%) is ACCEPTED and 48 (90.01%) BLOCKS, 500 lines removed (97.81%) is ACCEPTED and 570 (97.74%) BLOCKS -- the control proves the block is the FLOOR, not the fixture. AND NOTE THE GATE'S RESOLUTION so nothing wrong is expected of it: ~48 branches / ~570 lines. A SINGLE uncovered line CANNOT block this aggregate and is not meant to -- measured, one added uncovered line leaves the ratchet OK while scripts/diff-coverage.mjs BLOCKS it by name, which is the intended division of labour and what diff-coverage's own message states.
_optionsNotTaken: RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT REBUILT. (a) COVERING THE ~100 NEWLY-COUNTED BRANCHES is real work spread about ONE PER FILE across ~100 files; it genuinely improves the suite and remains worth doing, but it does not unblock main today and is a different task. (b) REMOVING THE TEST'S `reviewCommand` DRIVER IS MEASURED NOT TO WORK: a session did exactly that -- diff-coverage went green and the ratchet STILL read 90.16% -- because a shallow driver still ENTERS `reviewCommand`; no third shape was found. (c) CHANGING THE MECHANISM -- a tolerance band at a stated multiple of measured noise, or a floor that genuinely ratchets on green -- REMAINS OPEN, IS BETTER ENGINEERING, and is carried by W1-T467; it is a larger build than this. NOTE WHAT TODAY'S GATE ACTUALLY IS: NOTHING IN THE REPO WRITES THIS FILE. scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs, src/lib/ci-parity.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml and four test suites only READ it, so the `ratchet` is a STATIC THRESHOLD plus a manual human ritual -- which is why it drifted for three weeks before #1564 and why it went red today.
